reason: A tool body that runs inside the host and ignores cancellation cannot be stopped by the host.
justification: Go runtime fact: no API stops a goroutine from outside, and running every first-party tool in its own process would cost a process start per call. DH-ADR-TOOLS-5 bounds the wait, settles the call as outcome unknown and lists the body as detached; third-party tool code runs out of process under DH-ADR-4.

reason: A policy listener cannot rewrite the arguments of a tool call.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-3: logged arguments are never rewritten, so that the log, the audit trail, the UI and the execution agree (outcome DH-O-6).

reason: The repeat reminder counts a parent and its subagent separately.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-9: a repeat chain describes one model's own context, and a subagent has a different context, so the two are not one loop.

reason: A todo list belongs to one agent session; there is no shared, subagent or team list.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: one owner per list keeps the event a last-write-wins snapshot. Shared work items are the team task board of DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-11, not this tool.

reason: A todo item is content plus one of three states, with no id, priority or active-form field.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: whole-list replacement needs no item identity and a smaller shape costs fewer tokens on every write.

reason: Replacing the whole list is the only todo operation.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: a whole-list event needs no merge and replays as last write wins, and the model already holds the list in its context.

reason: The vendor's version gate is evaluated in the client, so a modified client can request any model id.
justification: Fact of any client-side check: a program cannot enforce a rule on a modified copy of itself; only the vendor service can. The specification documents the gate as a compatibility guard, not a security control.

reason: The reasoning effort levels in the vendor's model listing are not read; levels come from the embedded catalogue.
justification: Still open (register entry U-K1-12): the shape of the listing field is not in the pinned upstream source. Section 10 of the spec now says that scenario DH-E-LLM-5 keeps one real listing and that a tolerant read is then added to the catalogue refresh of DH-ADR-LLM-6. What is missing: the steps and assertions of DH-E-LLM-5 do not mention the effort field, and no deliverable or test covers the read, so the fact is not obtained and the read is not designed.

reason: Images are input only and are sent as bytes the harness holds; a provider is never given a URL, and assistant image output is not supported.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-LLM-3 item (f): a URL the provider fetches would be model-visible content that is not in the session log. The upload-recovery half of the upstream bullet is removed by the time-based cool-down of DH-D-LLM-5.

reason: Token counts for text are a calibrated estimate, not an exact count.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-LLM-9: the meter is a deterministic fold of the log with no model call, and its tradeoff says a consumer that needs exact tokens must ask the provider. An exact local count would need a tokenizer per vendor, which not every vendor publishes.

reason: The log records the intent to run a tool, not the completion of its external effect.
justification: Fact of any system that acts on the outside world: a local log cannot be made atomic with an effect on another system, so after a crash the outcome of a started call is unknown. The call id is handed to tool bodies as an idempotency key and recovery reports outcome unknown (DH-D-STORE-4).

reason: Nothing is checkpointed inside a running model attempt, so a crash loses stream text that had not settled.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a disk sync per stream chunk is refused, and nothing model-visible is lost because the attempt never settled. DH-ADR-STORE-3 now states it (nothing is checkpointed inside a running model attempt), as does the failure table of design.md section 5.

reason: A tool call with no result is recorded as outcome unknown and is never retried automatically.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-10: retrying a call that may already have taken effect is the worse error, so the model is told to verify.

reason: A session-log upload acknowledged just before a crash can be sent again.
justification: Fact of an acknowledgement over HTTP: the sender cannot record the acceptance atomically with the receiver's reply, so delivery is at least once. Each event carries the session id and sequence number so the receiver can remove duplicates, and the acceptance is committed as soon as the writer is free (DH-D-STORE-9).

reason: Upstream stalls the upload behind an event larger than the byte limit. DH-ADR-STORE-10 now sends an elision record in its place (the event's sequence number, time, type, size and digest, marked omitted), so the uploaded log stays contiguous by number and continues (register entry U-K1-11; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner). Built by DH-D-STORE-9 and proven by DH-T-STORE-15. Whether the vendor accepts such a line is settled by scenario DH-E-STORE-4, the same exit gate as the Go log format itself; if the vendor refuses, the component is not shipped.
An interrupted turn is closed with synthetic closers and never continued.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-10 and design.md section 5: continuing would repeat a model request whose stream is lost and tools whose outcome is unknown.

reason: A transcript holds committed history only; stream text that has not settled into an event is absent.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a view reads committed events only (design.md section 4.6, DH-ADR-VIEW-1). The silent part of the upstream limit is removed by DH-D-VIEW-8, which states the cut and marks an open turn. DH-ADR-VIEW-9 now states the committed-only rule (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Only explicitly marked lines are quotes; Markdown lazy continuation is not implemented.
justification: Deliberate boundary: with lazy continuation the text a user types after a quote would be shown as part of the quote. The fenced-code half is removed by DH-D-VIEW-8. DH-ADR-VIEW-9 now states the rule (a quote is a line that carries the quote mark and nothing else is; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner), and test DH-T-VIEW-20 pins it.

reason: Upstream's hazard was that a client could read the presence of a projection key as a statement about one session's capabilities. In the Go design no reader can do that: the host renders pages, a read names its keys and an unknown key is an error, and whether a feature is on is asked of the composition. The host-wide fold table that remains is the design, not a limit.
With the default cadence a title is generated once from the first message and can stop describing a long session.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-VIEW-6 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: the default first-prompt cadence titles a session once and never retitles it automatically; Refresh or the every-prompt cadence is the remedy, because one bounded model call per session is the cost the product chose). The remedies are built by DH-D-VIEW-4.

reason: When the current directory and the original project are both gone, every model turn is rejected until a person chooses a directory.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-VIEW-8: the write boundary is resolved from the directory, so guessing one would not fail closed. The dead end is removed: DH-D-VIEW-10 returns a typed error on which every carrier offers the choice of an existing directory.

reason: Changes to ignored files and to files outside the working directory are listed only when a file tool made them.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-FS-11 item (e): walking ignored trees every turn costs more than it tells, and files outside the write roots cannot be enumerated. The event's coverage field and the card say so (DH-D-FS-9).

reason: Edits and patches work on UTF-8 text and on UTF-16 text that starts with a byte-order mark; files in any other encoding are not edited as text. A plain move accepts any file.
justification: Narrowed, then kept on purpose. The re-sweep's gap (U-K1-14) is removed: DH-ADR-FS-11 item (a) now has fsx decode a UTF-16 file with a byte-order mark, edit the decoded text and write it back in the same byte order with the same mark and line endings, the version digest staying over the bytes on disk (DH-D-FS-1, DH-D-FS-6, test DH-T-FS-27). What remains is stated by the same record as its scope boundary: other encodings without a mark are not read as text, because without a mark the encoding is a guess and a literal match against a guessed decoding can edit the wrong bytes.

reason: A move that must not replace its destination, applies hunks or crosses write roots is two effects, not one atomic step.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-FS-11 item (c): the rooted handles the fence requires (os.Root) offer no rename that refuses to replace, and a rename across filesystems is never atomic. The outcome states both effects (DH-D-FS-4).

reason: Copy and recursive directory operations are not part of the file provider contract.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-FS-11: no model-facing tool needs them and the shell covers them under the process sandbox. The racy separate link check of the upstream bullet is removed by the do-not-follow option of DH-D-FS-4.

reason: A patch that fails part-way is not rolled back; the report lists every operation as completed, failed, unknown or not executed.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-FS-11 item (b): undoing earlier operations could overwrite an edit made from outside in the meantime.

reason: The read tool reads UTF-8 text and UTF-16 text with a byte-order mark; other unmarked encodings, audio and video are not read as text.
justification: Narrowed, then kept on purpose. A UTF-16 file with a byte-order mark is now read through the same decoding (DH-ADR-FS-11 item (a), DH-D-FS-6, test DH-T-FS-27; the re-sweep's U-K1-14). The record states the rest as its scope boundary in its own words: other encodings without a mark, audio and video are not read as text, because without a mark the encoding is a guess; audio and video never reach a model by DH-ADR-LLM-1, and a non-text file is answered with the name of the tool that reads it.

reason: The single-editor tool handles UTF-8 text and UTF-16 text with a byte-order mark; other encodings are not edited as text.
justification: The same as unit fs.fs.1: DH-ADR-FS-11 item (a) names str_replace_editor among the operations that work on decoded UTF-16 text with a mark, and states unmarked encodings as its scope boundary. Note: test DH-T-FS-27 exercises read, edit and apply_patch, not this tool, which shares the decoding of fsx and is built later (DH-D-FS-8).

reason: str_replace requires exactly one match and has no replace_all argument.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-FS-11 item (d): the tool exists for the schema some models already know, so it is not extended; the edit tool offers replace_all.

reason: A process tree is owned by the operating system on Windows and on Linux; on macOS, and on a Linux host that has neither a writable cgroup nor a user service manager, it falls back to process groups.
justification: macOS fact: the system offers no persistent owner for a range of processes. The Linux half that the review tracked as U-K1-1 is removed by the design: DH-ADR-EXEC-2 now has the host ask the user service manager once at start for a delegated scope (owner decision DH-ADR-40), built by DH-D-EXEC-2 and proven by test DH-T-EXEC-17 and scenario DH-E-EXEC-10 on a real SSH login. A Linux host with no user manager, such as a bare container, keeps the fallback and says so on every handle.

reason: On Windows an interrupt is the Ctrl-C input byte, which the console delivers to every attached process; stop and hang-up signals do not exist.
justification: Windows console fact: there are no per-process-group job-control signals, so no terminal library can deliver them. The backend refuses the unsupported signals instead of ignoring them (DH-D-EXEC-5).

reason: Where only process groups own a terminal's children, a child that leaves the terminal session before it is observed can escape cleanup.
justification: macOS fact: process groups and sessions are the strongest owners the system offers, and a process-table scan sees only a moment. On Linux the gap is closed where a control group is available, which now includes a scope delegated by the user service manager (DH-ADR-EXEC-2, register entry U-K1-1). Survivors are reported, not hidden (DH-ADR-EXEC-2).

reason: Secrets are removed from a child's environment by name pattern, so a secret with an unusual name in the operator's own environment still reaches the child.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-8 (tradeoff: the scrub is still a name heuristic for secrets the harness does not know) and accepted by DH-ADR-SECURITY-6. Deny and allow patterns are configuration, so an operator who wants a closed list can deny everything and allow named variables; names the configuration uses as credential references are removed exactly.

reason: Terminal sessions and their screen state live in the host process and end with it.
justification: Deliberate boundary: DH-ADR-EXEC-2 has the host hold every tree owner so that no child runs unowned, and DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4 says nothing is installed to keep a process alive. Surviving a restart would need a supervisor outside the host. The model's input and the returned output stay durable as tool events.

reason: A terminal session has exactly one owning agent and cannot be shared with or transferred to another agent.
justification: Deliberate boundary: owner scoping is the access rule that keeps one agent out of another agent's terminal; a person may attach a browser and take control, which the same decision governs. Stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-9 item (a) (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: A terminal session is created only on request, by an agent tool call or by a user in the web terminal; configuration cannot start one.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a session needs an owner whose end closes it, and an owner exists only once an agent or a user asks. Stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-9 item (c) (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: That a foreign child process is waiting for terminal input can be proven on Linux only; elsewhere readiness is inferred.
justification: Operating-system fact: macOS and Windows offer no facility that proves another process is blocked reading the terminal. The Go design narrows the limit (a bracketed command completes exactly on every system) and reports the uncertain case as inferred_idle (DH-D-EXEC-7).

reason: A host restart destroys every terminal session.
justification: The same deliberate boundary as unit terminal.terminal.1: DH-ADR-EXEC-2 ends children with the host on purpose so that nothing runs unowned, and DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4 installs nothing that outlives the host.

reason: Confinement governs file effects, and the network where a backend can enforce it; process visibility is not governed uniformly.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3, whose scope sentence names this unit (nothing is promised about which processes a command may see or signal), and by DH-ADR-SECURITY-10 (a confined command can still see and signal other processes of the same user).

reason: A denied file operation inside a confined command is inferred from the command's stderr and reported only as a hint.
justification: Classed a platform limit before, but the fact was asserted without a source per backend, as the debt audit found (Q3-3), and it may not hold everywhere. Inference, not verified: Landlock reports a denial only through the kernel audit subsystem, which needs privileges; the Windows token reports one only through object-access auditing, which needs an administrator; but macOS writes sandbox violations to the unified system log, which the user can read, so a typed denial report may be possible there. Since the final re-check, areas/sandbox-ssh.md holds the claim as an assumption to settle per backend by three named scenarios (DH-E-SANDBOX-1 for bubblewrap and Landlock, DH-E-SANDBOX-4 for the Windows token, DH-E-SANDBOX-3 for macOS), and the macOS backend reads the sandbox log as a hint, kept only if DH-E-SANDBOX-3 shows the records name the process. What is still missing: the facts themselves; none of the scenarios has run, so no source can be named yet. Whether the launcher itself failed is no longer inferred (DH-ADR-SECURITY-3).

reason: A PowerShell command is text that PowerShell itself parses, so a syntax error is a command failure and not a launch failure.
justification: Fact of PowerShell: the shell is the only parser of its language, and a second parser in the harness could disagree with it. This is what a shell tool is, and DH-ADR-EXEC-7 keeps it with no translation layer.

reason: Non-ASCII standard input can be mis-decoded when the resolved shell is Windows PowerShell 5.1.
justification: Still open until one measurement is taken (register entry U-K1-12): scenario DH-E-EXEC-7 now passes non-ASCII text on standard input to Windows PowerShell 5.1 started with its console input code page set to UTF-8 and records the outcome. If the text arrives intact the limit is resolved by setting the code page before start; if not, it is a platform limit of that edition. What is missing: the scenario has not run, and the executor does not yet set the code page on this path. Impact is small: only the 5.1 fallback and only in-process callers that pass stdin.

reason: Reads are not confined on Windows.
justification: Windows fact: the write-restricted token that DH-ADR-SECURITY-2 keeps intersects write access only (WRITE_RESTRICTED), so it cannot deny a read. The one unprivileged alternative, an AppContainer, needs a read grant on every path the child reads, the compilers and tools included, which upstream measured and rejected (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/README.md:125, :160). The same fact as sandbox unit sandbox-windows-acl.8; every result reports enforcement partial. The review first classed this row as a scope boundary, but no decision record states that reads are unconfined: design.md section 6 says it, outside a record.

reason: Windows read-only mode is a partial boundary: hard links alias a file across paths, and trees that another sandbox stamped with a package identifier are unreadable.
justification: Windows fact: NTFS hard links give one file several paths, and the access rules for Low-integrity tokens and package identifiers are the kernel's. No unprivileged Windows mechanism removes them (DH-ADR-SECURITY-2); every start reports partial with the named effects (DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3).

reason: The persistent bash tool needs an owning agent and a real pseudo-terminal; without them it reports unavailable.
justification: Deliberate boundary: the owner gives the shell its lifetime and its access rule, and persistent shell state needs a terminal. Stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-9 items (a) and (d) (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner): where no pseudo-terminal can be allocated the tools report unavailable and never fall back to pipes.

reason: A foreground child that waits for input is recognised exactly on Linux only; elsewhere the call runs to its timeout.
justification: Operating-system fact, the same as unit terminal-bash.2: macOS and Windows cannot prove that a foreign process is blocked reading the terminal. A following command is refused while the previous one has not finished, so nothing is typed into the child (DH-ADR-EXEC-6).

reason: The persistent PowerShell tool needs an owning agent and a pseudo-terminal backend with the pwsh dialect; without them it reports unavailable.
justification: Deliberate boundary, the same as for the bash twin: the owner gives the shell its lifetime and access rule. Stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-9 items (a) and (d) (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner): where no pseudo-terminal can be allocated the tools report unavailable and never fall back to pipes.

reason: Stop and hang-up signals are unavailable on Windows and an interrupt is a console-wide Ctrl-C, which at a prompt cancels the pending line.
justification: Windows console fact, the same as unit subprocess-local.5: consoles have no per-process-group signals. The backend refuses the unsupported signals and the result says so (DH-D-EXEC-5).

reason: A terminal bell is not reported to the model.
justification: Deliberate boundary: nothing consumes a bell and a model-facing channel for terminal decoration would spend tokens without a use. Stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-9 item (e) (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Under the Windows sandbox a confined command cannot open named pipes.
justification: Windows fact: a new named pipe gets a default security descriptor that no restricting identifier satisfies (see sandbox unit sandbox-windows-acl.6). The language-mode half of the upstream bullet is no longer carried: the execution spec now carries named pipes only, DH-ADR-SANDBOX-4 gives read-only mode a private scratch directory so that PowerShell is expected to start in its full mode (to be confirmed by scenario DH-E-SANDBOX-4), and nothing in the design relies on the reduced mode.

reason: The model must write PowerShell for the pwsh tool and bash for the bash tool; nothing translates between them.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-EXEC-7 (a registry by dialect, with no translation): translation between shell languages cannot be made correct in general, and both tools may be mounted on one system.

reason: On Windows hard-link aliases, unconfined reads and trees stamped by another sandbox are outside what the restricted token can govern.
justification: Windows fact: these are properties of the write-restricted Low-integrity token, the only unprivileged mechanism that does not need a read grant on every path (DH-ADR-SECURITY-2). Every start reports partial with the named effects and a policy that requires full is refused (DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3).

reason: An older Linux kernel governs only the Landlock access kinds it knows, so enforcement there is partial.
justification: Linux kernel fact: the Landlock ABI version of the running kernel decides which access kinds exist, and user space cannot add one. The state is computed per start, the missing kinds are named, and a policy that requires full is refused (DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3).

reason: The macOS backend depends on the deprecated sandbox-exec program.
justification: macOS fact: Apple offers a command-line program no supported, unprivileged successor for confining a child process (DH-ADR-SECURITY-2). The backend is probed at every start-up, so removal by Apple shows as unavailable before the first command and confined modes fail closed (DH-D-SANDBOX-5).

reason: The sandbox policy has a file mode and a network setting but no knob for process policy.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3, whose scope sentence names this unit, and by DH-ADR-SECURITY-10 (exactly two dimensions; processes, system calls and devices are outside), the same as unit sandbox.1.

reason: A program confined by the Windows token cannot give its own children named-pipe standard streams.
justification: Windows fact: a new named pipe gets a default security descriptor that no restricting identifier satisfies, and adding the user's own identifier to the token would remove the write restriction. Inherited and anonymous pipes work, and the model-visible policy text says so (DH-D-SANDBOX-6).

reason: The first access grant on a directory walks every descendant, which can take tens of seconds on a large tree.
justification: Windows fact: the system propagates inheritable access entries eagerly, and the confined child needs the inherited entries. DH-ADR-SANDBOX-6 moves the cost to the one-time consent step, with progress and cancellation, so it never runs inside a command's time limit.

reason: The Windows token restricts writes only; reads are unconfined and sockets cannot be restricted.
justification: Windows fact: WRITE_RESTRICTED intersects write access only and the mechanism has no socket control. A policy with the network denied fails closed on Windows instead of running unconfined (DH-ADR-SECURITY-10).

reason: A Low-integrity child cannot read objects that another AppContainer-based tool stamped with a package identifier.
justification: Windows kernel access rule outside the harness's control. The doctor command names the affected objects and offers the repair to the directory's owner, and the limit is one of the named reasons for partial enforcement (DH-ADR-SANDBOX-6).

reason: The sandbox policy expresses file effects and a network setting; it expresses no process, system-call or device restriction.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated in their own words by DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3 (Scope boundary of this record: a policy promises file effects, the network setting, the protection of the harness home and delegated-execution, and nothing about which processes a command may see or signal, which system calls it may make, or which devices it may open; a product choice, not a platform limit, because a dimension only one backend enforces would read partial on every other) and by DH-ADR-SECURITY-10 (the policy has exactly two dimensions, file effects and network).

reason: A file-effect denial inside a spawned command is inferred from the command's stderr.
justification: The same claim as execution unit bash-sandbox.2, asserted without a source per backend (audit finding Q3-3); on macOS the unified system log may carry a typed violation record the user can read (inference, not verified). The seam keeps one classifier, labels its result a hint that never changes the exit code, and file tools, which run in the host, return typed denials (DH-D-SANDBOX-3). The specification now names the three scenarios that settle the claim per backend (DH-E-SANDBOX-1, -3, -4) and reads the macOS sandbox log as a hint if DH-E-SANDBOX-3 shows it names the process. What is still missing: the facts; no scenario has run.

reason: Remote confinement does not restrict process visibility, and a remote backend that is partial stays partial.
justification: The remote host runs the same operating-system backends with the same limits as a local host, so the facts of the remote kernel apply unchanged. The network setting is enforced remotely and the remote confinement state is reported on every result (DH-D-SANDBOX-9, DH-ADR-SANDBOX-3).

reason: The SSH host and the helper installed on it are trusted infrastructure.
justification: Fact of remote execution: the remote machine executes every file and process request it is sent, so no client-side design makes a hostile host safe. The digest check of DH-ADR-SANDBOX-8 detects a wrong or stale helper only; the trust statement is shown at connect.

reason: A tool body called from a script runs in the host and may allocate memory while producing its result, before any size bound applies.
justification: Go runtime fact: memory cannot be limited per goroutine, so a pipeline can bound only what a body returns. Each first-party body must bound its own reads (for file tools DH-ADR-FS-8 does); the register recommends a conformance check for this beside the cancellation check of DH-ADR-TOOLS-5.

reason: A script is exactly as confined as the sandbox backend of its platform: enforcement is full or partial and reads are unconfined.
justification: Inherited operating-system facts (see the sandbox units: Windows is always partial, old Linux kernels are partial). This area cannot strengthen a backend; it reports mode, backend and enforcement in workflow/run-start and in the tool result (DH-D-PTC-2).

reason: On macOS, and on a Linux host without a delegated control group, a script's process tree has no memory or process-count limit; processor use is bounded by run time only.
justification: macOS fact: it has no facility that limits the memory of a tree of processes. Elsewhere the gap the review tracked as U-K1-2 is removed by the design: DH-ADR-PTC-5 gives a workflow run a memory and a process-count limit (maxMemoryBytes, maxProcesses), passed as Spec.Limits and carried out by the job object or control group of DH-D-EXEC-2 (test DH-T-EXEC-17, scenario DH-E-EXEC-10); the run record says enforced, partial or unavailable. No processor meter is added: the run budget of DH-ADR-PTC-5 bounds elapsed time.

reason: Cleanup of a script's process tree is as good as the tree owner of the platform; on macOS a process that leaves its process group can escape.
justification: macOS fact: process groups are the strongest owner the system offers. On Linux the gap is closed where a control group is available, which now includes a scope delegated by the user service manager (DH-ADR-EXEC-2). The run record says cleanup incomplete and names survivors instead of claiming a clean stop (DH-ADR-PTC-4).

reason: Subagent provider, caps and tool name of a workflow are deployment configuration; the model may lower two caps for one call and never raise them.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-PTC-5: a cap the model could raise is not a cap.

reason: A workflow script's file confinement and process cleanup inherit the limits of the sandbox backend and of the process-tree owner on each platform.
justification: Inherited operating-system facts owned by the sandbox and execution areas (see units ptc-runtime-node.2 and ptc-runtime-node.4). Enforcement facts are in workflow/run-start, and an unconfirmed cleanup ends the run as cleanup incomplete with named survivors (DH-ADR-PTC-4).

reason: A workflow run cannot be continued after a process restart; an open run is closed as interrupted.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-PTC-6: a script's direct effects are not recorded call by call, so re-running it could repeat them. Members and their outcomes are durable (DH-D-PTC-3), so the model can write a new script that skips finished members.

reason: A workflow script cannot start another workflow.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-TOOLS-6 (a command started by a nested call receives no call token, which keeps attribution to one outer call) and DH-ADR-PTC-3. The saved half of the upstream bullet is removed by the file argument of DH-D-PTC-4, and a member agent whose preset has the workflow tool can start its own run within the subagent depth limit.

reason: Each ACP delegation starts one fresh agent process and pays the handshake; there is no process pool.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (tradeoff: an external child still gets one process per run): one process per run is what lets the run own the whole process tree and prove it gone before the result is released.

reason: An ACP child receives a local path and runs on the host's own machine; a child on a remote machine is not offered.
justification: Deliberate boundary now stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (a child never runs on a remote machine; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner): no area designs the mapping of paths, credentials and process ownership to a second machine, and a remote workspace is reached through the execution world of the child's tools, not by moving the child.

reason: A harness agent preset and harness model options cannot be applied inside a foreign ACP agent; a request that needs them is refused at admission.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: a foreign product, an ACP agent, Codex or Claude Code, runs with its own operator configuration and takes no harness preset and no per-call model option, because the harness cannot compose prompts, tools or models inside another product). The output-schema and depth halves of the upstream bullet are removed by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9 and DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-4.

reason: Only the ACP agent's final text, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic enter the parent's log.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9: a child's working trace must not enter its creator's model context or log. Other updates are offered to a view as an unlogged progress event.

reason: Each Claude Code delegation is one fresh process with no saved session, continuation or pool.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (one process per run) and by library decision DH-ADR-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-1, which turns session persistence off so that none of the product's state is left to clean up.

reason: The harness does not create an account, log in or edit Claude Code settings; a sign-in failure is reported with its stage.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 (external products run as the operator installed them) and DH-ADR-SECURITY-6: account state belongs to the vendor's product and the user.

reason: A Claude Code child cannot ask a person: permission prompts are denied and questions are unavailable to it.
justification: Not a platform limit, as the debt audit found (Q3-3): the vendor's SDK has prompt callbacks, and the limit follows from the driver the design chose. DH-ADR-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-1 now states it as a scope boundary of that record, in its options table: no permission callback follows from driving print mode, so the external agent has no path to ask the user. The same record names a lead to check before the first build (a flag that hands permission prompts to an MCP tool in print mode); if DH-E-CLAUDEAGENTSDK-1 shows it works, the driver uses it and the boundary narrows. A user who needs prompts reaches Claude Code through the ACP provider (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7: Claude Code cannot ask a person).

reason: Only the final answer, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic enter the parent's log; reasoning, tool traffic and stderr do not.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9: a child's reasoning, tool traffic and stderr, which may hold secrets, must not enter its creator's model context. Usage is added to the settled record when the product reports it.

reason: A harness preset and a per-call model choice are refused for a Claude Code child.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 in its own words (a foreign product takes no harness preset and no per-call model option); DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 fixes the mode in the instance configuration, and tool targets give the choice among instances. The output-schema and depth halves are removed by the manager.

reason: Upstream has no time limit and restores nothing. In the Go design every external instance has maxDuration (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7), and a target configured with isolation: worktree (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the resolution of register entry U-K1-3) runs the child, local or external, in its own checkout on its own branch, so a cancelled or failed run leaves the user's working tree untouched and the branch is the rollback. DH-T-SUBAGENT-32 covers the option and scenario DH-E-SUBAGENT-7 cancels an external run half-way and checks the user's tree. Remainder: the option is off by default, by the owner's decision DH-ADR-40, so in the default configuration a cancelled run still leaves its edits in the user's tree; effects outside the checkout are never undone, which is a fact and not debt. Built by DH-D-SUBAGENT-10.
Each Codex delegation is one fresh process, one unsaved thread and one turn, with no continuation or pool.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (one process per run) and by library decision DH-ADR-CODEX-1, which keeps the thread unsaved so that nothing of the product's state is left behind.

reason: The harness does not create an account, log in, trust a project or edit Codex settings.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7 and DH-ADR-SECURITY-6: account and project-trust state belong to the vendor's product and the user. A failure the product reports with status 401 or 403 gets the category auth.

reason: Only the selected answer, bounded, and a fixed-word diagnostic enter the parent's log.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-9, the same as for the Claude Code child.

reason: A harness preset and a per-call model choice are refused for a Codex child.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 in its own words (a foreign product, Codex included, takes no harness preset and no per-call model option), the same as for the Claude Code child.

reason: Upstream has no time limit and restores nothing. In the Go design every external instance has maxDuration (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-7), and a target configured with isolation: worktree (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the resolution of register entry U-K1-3) runs the Codex child in its own checkout on its own branch, so a cancelled or failed run leaves the user's working tree untouched and the branch is the rollback. DH-T-SUBAGENT-32 covers the option, and scenario DH-E-SUBAGENT-7 cancels a real Codex run half-way and checks the user's tree. Remainder: the option is off by default, by the owner's decision DH-ADR-40, so in the default configuration a cancelled run still leaves its edits in the user's tree; effects outside the checkout are never undone, which is a fact and not debt. Built by DH-D-SUBAGENT-10.
Each SDK delegation starts one fresh dsh runtime, which boots a whole component tree; there is no pool.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (one process per run). A task that does not need process isolation uses the in-process providers.

reason: The SDK child runs as a local process in a local directory; a remote runtime is not offered.
justification: The same boundary as unit subagent-acp.2, now stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (a child never runs on a remote machine; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: A fork child sees its creator's completed turns as of the fork and nothing the creator logs later.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-10 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: a fork copies the creator's completed turns once, when it starts, and never follows the creator's later turns, because a child is its own independent log and a single copy keeps the provider's cached prefix). A creator that wants to share more sends a message.

reason: The shipped fork tools offer no model route fields.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-10 (fork inherits and offers no route fields by default): a provider's prefix cache is keyed by model, so a fork on another model cannot reuse the inherited prefix that fork exists for. An operator may turn the fields on.

reason: A spawn child starts with none of its creator's conversation.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-10 in its own words (a spawn starts with an empty conversation); the fork provider exists for the other case, and merging them would make every delegation pay for the inherited history.

reason: A child's name cannot be changed or reused once the child was published.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-4 (names are unique for ever among one creator's children, except that a start that never published frees its name): a name appears in logged messages, notices and task owner fields, and reuse would make that history ambiguous.

reason: An ACP agent, Codex or Claude Code child runs once and accepts no follow-up message; the dsh runtime child now accepts one.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-5 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner): a follow-up to an external child is a second run in a new process, offered where the child has a durable session. The dsh runtime provider is now Continuable (DH-D-SUBAGENT-7, test DH-T-SUBAGENT-33), which is what register entry U-K1-4 recommended. ACP children become continuable later, where the agent can load a session; Codex and Claude Code stay single-run because their library decisions turn saved sessions off.

reason: A model-authored message stays within one agent tree and reaches only the root or a local member.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-8 (tradeoff: no message crosses trees): tree membership is the only authority for a model-authored message. A person can prompt any session they may access.

reason: send_message returns a receipt and never the target's reply.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-8 (a send has a receipt, never a reply): a reply cannot be attributed to one message once several messages share a step. A caller that wants a return value starts a child with wait.

reason: The shipped fork tools leave model selection off.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-10, the same as unit subagent-fork-in-process.3; an operator may turn the option on under the same route authorisation.

reason: Upstream gives members no worktree. In the Go design a delegation target may be configured with isolation: worktree (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the owner's resolution of register entry U-K1-3 in DH-ADR-40): the manager calls worktree.Service.ForChild before the child exists, and the child, local or external, works on its own branch in its own checkout as its only write root. It is off by default, works only in a Git repository with the worktree component mounted, and nothing is merged automatically; without it members share one checkout. Remainder: in the default configuration members still share one checkout, by the owner's decision DH-ADR-40 (off by default), not by omission. Built by DH-D-SUBAGENT-10; proven by DH-T-SUBAGENT-32, DH-T-XFORGE-13 and scenario DH-E-SUBAGENT-7.
In a shared checkout a member's write scopes only warn; a shell command, a formatter or a generator can write outside them.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-11 (tradeoff: write scopes stay advisory in a shared checkout, and the views say not enforced). The enforced alternative now exists: a member started with isolation: worktree has its own checkout as its only write root (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the resolution of register entry U-K1-3). Enforcing scopes inside a shared checkout is listed as not designed in section 10 of the spec.

reason: Members cannot message another team, and only an ancestor or the user can interrupt a member.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-8: tree membership is the only authority for a model-authored message, and ancestry the only one for a model-requested stop.

reason: The team policy text coordinates and does not confine: in a shared checkout it cannot stop a shell command or an external process from writing overlapping files.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-11: a prompt coordinates, and confinement is the sandbox's job. Members that must not collide are started with isolation: worktree, each in its own checkout (DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-12, the resolution of register entry U-K1-3).

reason: The job contract is in-process: live work cannot be handed to another process.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-1 (a job is owned by one session's agent and lives in the host process): a producer holds process handles, pipes and in-process state, and the design has no supervisor outside the host (DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4). DH-ADR-JOBS-4 records the loss in the session log.

reason: The model's cursor is the only consuming read of a job's output; observers read at their own offset without consuming.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-2: two consuming readers would each receive part of the output.

reason: Jobs and their in-memory output end with the host process; on resume each lost job is closed in the log and the model is told.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-1; DH-ADR-JOBS-4 and DH-D-JOBS-2 make the loss a recorded fact, and spilled output survives.

reason: The model tools are the single consuming reader of a job's stream; the UI follows a job without consuming.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-2, the same as unit jobs.jobs.2.

reason: A schedule fires only while a dsh process that fires schedules is running.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-WEBAPP-4 (the host is a foreground process the user owns; no service, login item or tray is installed) and narrowed by DH-ADR-JOBS-7: any firing host on the home can deliver, a failed delivery retries with back-off, and a late delivery reports how late it is and how many occurrences were missed (DH-ADR-JOBS-6).

reason: Schedule rules are five-field cron and a bounded subset of RFC 5545, and future occurrences depend on the machine's time-zone data.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-6 and DH-ADR-RRULE-1 for the rule subset. The zone-data half is a fact no design removes: governments change zone rules. Committed occurrences are stored as UTC and never move, and DH-ADR-TEMPORAL-1 reports the data source.

reason: The caller that records a goal as complete or blocked is authoritative; no independent evaluator ships.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-10 (tradeoff: the model still judges completion; the goal.Completing interception is a place for a deterministic check, not an evaluator).

reason: A session has at most one current goal and there is no goal database; history stays in the session log.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-9 (a goal is one event-sourced objective per session): parallel objectives are separate sessions or delegated agents.

reason: The model decides when evidence is sufficient and whether a blocker is unchanged; the runtime enforces only counts and budgets.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-10, the same as unit goal.goal.3.

reason: Goal rounds run in the same session; the driver starts no fresh agent and forks nothing.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-9: independent attempts with fresh context are delegation and workflows, which the subagent and workflow areas provide.

reason: Execution proves that the turn holds a direct human message on a root agent, not that the request merits a goal.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-9 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: the goal tool proves that a person spoke in the current turn, not that the request deserves a goal; judging merit needs an understanding the runtime does not have).

reason: The runtime enforces the number of consecutive rounds before a model-reported blocker, not that the obstacle is the same one.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-10 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: whether two reported blockers are the same obstacle is the model's judgement, and the runtime only counts rounds and enforces the round cap and budgets, because counting is exact).

reason: A subagent in plan mode cannot open the plan review; it returns its plan as its result to the parent that asked.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-JOBS-11: a child's plan is reviewed by its parent, which presents it to the person; a review channel per child would put several reviews before one person with no order.

reason: The compaction trigger rests on an estimated token count, not an exact one.
justification: Deliberate boundary inherited from DH-ADR-LLM-9 (the meter is a deterministic fold with no model call). DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4 bounds the effect: the threshold keeps headroom below the window, and provider-confirmed overflow recovery is the backstop.

reason: A system prompt plus tool list that alone approaches the context window cannot be shrunk by compaction.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4 (the system prompt node is never in a span): compaction acts on history, and the envelope is fixed by composition. The engine reports compact/envelope-too-large with both sizes. The single-oversized-unit half of the upstream bullet is removed by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-5.

reason: An offloaded image stays offloaded when a budget grows or history shrinks.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6 (an offloaded image is never restored automatically): automatic restore would make the model-visible image set depend on unlogged request preparation. The placeholder names a read-only path, and reading it creates a new logged occurrence.

reason: A route with a small image budget, used briefly, offloads images for the rest of the session.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by the tradeoff of DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6 (a brief small-budget route offloads for good): an omission, once logged, holds for every later request. The image bytes are kept and can be read again.

reason: Prune budgets are character counts, not token counts.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a character budget makes pruning a pure, idempotent function, which a token estimate that moves with calibration would not guarantee. DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6 now states it in its tradeoff (prune budgets are counted in characters, not tokens, by this decision).

reason: Pruning keeps the head and the tail of a tool result without judging which middle lines matter.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by the tradeoff of DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6 (pruning is syntactic): a reduction without a model call cannot rank lines. The marker states how much was removed and where the full text is, and the original stays in the log.

reason: A prune cut can still split a grapheme cluster in rare cases.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6: a cut snaps to a line boundary where one lies inside the budget and is otherwise never placed before a combining mark, a variation selector or a joiner. Full Unicode segmentation is not a platform limit, only a module the design chose not to add for a cosmetic gain; the original text is in the log.

reason: There is no model-facing compaction tool; people compact through the command and pressure triggers it automatically.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4 (there is no model-facing compaction tool): a model that could compact at will could discard history the user relies on. DH-ADR-CONTEXT-10 gives the model read-only recall of compacted spans later.

reason: A system prompt plus tool list that alone approaches the window is reported, not compacted.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4, the same as unit compaction-basic.5; deferred tool disclosure in the tools area is the mechanism that shrinks a tool list.

reason: A change of directory that begins and ends inside one shell command triggers no discovery of nested instruction files.
justification: Fact of shells: what a command does inside the shell process is seen by no observer outside it. The lasting case that the review tracked as U-K1-10 is removed by the design: a persistent shell's end line carries its working directory (DH-ADR-EXEC-6), the tool result has a cwd field, and a changed cwd is a trigger in DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2 (DH-D-CONTEXT-2, test DH-T-CONTEXT-6). A shell call's working-directory argument also counts as a touch.

reason: Lower-case file names, rule directories and @path imports are not interpreted in instruction files.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2 (no @path imports, no rule directories): an import would let a repository file pull arbitrary paths into the prompt. Other file names are available through the candidates configuration field.

reason: Instruction text is bounded and truncated, never summarised by a model.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2 (no summarising of instruction text): summarising would add a model call to every session start and make the guidance differ from the file the user wrote.

reason: The file-mention index is bounded and omits excluded or unreadable directories.
justification: Deliberate boundary required by outcome DH-O-14 (anything that grows is bounded) and narrowed by DH-D-CONTEXT-4: ignore files shrink the index, a query with a slash lists the live directory whatever the bound, and the result carries a truncated flag. DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9 now states it (the file-mention index is bounded by this decision and says when it is incomplete).

reason: A mentioned file is text; its content enters the conversation only when the model reads it.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9 (a file mention stays text): content then arrives as a logged tool result under the read tool's bounds. A user who wants content attached uses attachments.

reason: A release that changes system-prompt text rewrites the first system message on routes that cannot take an in-history prompt update.
justification: Fact of model provider interfaces: the system prompt is the head of every request, so changing it changes the prefix a provider caches, and only some protocols accept a prompt update inside history. The package itself is not built (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3); the rewrite is a logged new request series, and no per-process value may enter the prompt (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-1).

reason: Only the text of user and assistant messages crosses from one session into another.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9 (tradeoff: images and tool results do not cross sessions): tool output from another session is the least trustworthy content to import.

reason: A session reference is a snapshot, not a live link.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9 (a reference is a pointer or a snapshot, never a live link): the snapshot in the target's log keeps its replay independent of the source session.

reason: The time-zone reading guides interpretation; it never fills another tool's zone argument.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a tool that needs a zone must receive it explicitly so that the logged arguments say what was scheduled. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (no tool takes a hidden zone argument; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: A turn holding prompts from different time zones tells the model to ask instead of guessing.
justification: Deliberate boundary: guessing which zone owns an unqualified time is the error this context exists to prevent. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Clock readings show whole seconds.
justification: Deliberate boundary: sub-second digits cost tokens in every reading and no tool consumes them; event times in the log keep full precision. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Clock readings accumulate in history between compactions.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by the tradeoff of DH-ADR-CONTEXT-1 (context costs history tokens until compaction): history is append-only so that the provider's prefix cache stays valid. The cost is bounded by the ten-minute default interval and by mounting the contributor only where it is used.

reason: The terminal location is read on the first step of a turn only.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a reading costs a process start and a pane rarely moves inside a turn. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Only the agent's own pane location is reported; the text of sibling panes is never read.
justification: Deliberate boundary and a guarantee: sibling panes may hold secrets, which outcome DH-O-7 keeps out of the log. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (the host's own pane only; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner) and pinned by a test.

reason: The pane layout tree is reported, not pixel sizes.
justification: Deliberate boundary: sizes change on every resize and would defeat the rule that an unchanged location adds no message. Stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-11 (recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: Detection of a tmux pane relies on the POSIX controlling terminal; on Windows the contributor does nothing.
justification: Third-party and operating-system fact: tmux does not run natively on Windows, and matching the controlling terminal is the only way to exclude a terminal that merely inherited tmux's environment variables. The contributor is off by default (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3 keeps it at low priority).

reason: Skill discovery is one directory level deep.
justification: Deliberate boundary: it bounds the scan, matches the layout other agent tools use for a shared skills directory, and keeps skill names unambiguous. DH-ADR-CONTEXT-7 now states it (discovery reads one directory level under each root).

reason: The office skills install no authoring libraries.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by the tradeoff of DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3 (authoring libraries are the user's to install) and by owner decision DH-ADR-20: the harness downloads and bundles nothing.

reason: LibreOffice output can differ from native Microsoft Office applications.
justification: Third-party fact: LibreOffice and Microsoft Office are different layout engines, and owner decision DH-ADR-20 fixes LibreOffice as the engine. The skill text states the difference and the document area reports the engine version with each result.

reason: Legacy, encrypted and macro-enabled office files need a separate workflow.
justification: Deliberate boundary now stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-7 (the Office skills do not cover encrypted or macro-enabled documents, which the office tools refuse); legacy files are converted first through the document area's convert tool.

reason: Loading a skill returns one text result, with no partial or streaming form.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-8 (a body over the size cap is refused with its size and path, never truncated) and DH-ADR-CONTEXT-7 (providers are asked under a deadline): a larger body is read in pages with the file tools from the reported path.

reason: The model is told a vendor CLI's absolute path but nothing enforces it; a command that names the CLI by bare name runs whatever PATH resolves.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONNECT-10 (the harness changes no command environment): a private PATH would hide the user's own installation. A hint with the registered path follows a shell result that failed to find the bare name (DH-D-CONNECT-9).

reason: A paid Linear workspace can require an administrator to approve the application before a user can grant access.
justification: Third-party fact: it is a policy of the Linear service, documented by Linear, that no client design removes. The account view shows the service's refusal so the user knows to ask an administrator and connect again (DH-D-CONNECT-4).

reason: Upstream offers four read-only operations. DH-ADR-CONNECT-7 now adds three more at lower priority: the symbols of one file, a symbol by name in the workspace, and the diagnostics of one file, which are fresh or marked stale (register entry U-K1-6). Built by DH-D-CONNECT-5; proven by DH-T-CONNECT-21 and by a diagnostics query after an edit in scenario DH-E-CONNECT-4. Remainder, kept as a scope boundary stated in the tradeoff of the same decision: edits (rename, code actions, formatting), because each needs a preview and a write-policy design, and the call hierarchy.
A language server may return empty or partial results while it indexes, and the tool promises no completeness across servers.
justification: Third-party and protocol fact: indexing is internal to each language server and the Language Server Protocol has no completeness signal. The provider tracks the server's progress notices and the result says when the server reported that it was still indexing (DH-ADR-CONNECT-7).

reason: MCP resources are read on demand only; a resource subscription is not followed.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONNECT-4: a changed resource is seen at the next read, and a pushed change notice is left as a later step that first needs a cap on how often a noisy server may cause a message. The other half of the upstream bullet is removed: each prompt a server offers is now a human command in the command registry (DH-D-CONNECT-3, test DH-T-CONNECT-22; register entry U-K1-7).

reason: Audio and other non-image binary payloads from an MCP tool reach the model only as a diagnostic line.
justification: Deliberate boundary of the model vocabulary: DH-ADR-LLM-1 keeps one closed vocabulary and it has no audio block, so there is nothing to project audio into. The embedded-text and image halves are removed by DH-D-CONNECT-3. DH-ADR-LLM-1 now says so in words (audio and video never reach a model, by this decision and not by omission; recommended default, not confirmed by the owner).

reason: An MCP result that violates the protocol or the tool's advertised output schema is refused; no legacy substitute is accepted.
justification: Deliberate strictness: DH-ADR-CONNECT-2 treats a server as untrusted and DH-ADR-CONNECT-4 routes MCP tools through the pipeline's validation. The failure has its own code, mcp/invalid-result. DH-ADR-CONNECT-4 now states it (a result that does not match the protocol's shape is refused whole, never read leniently).

reason: An MCP tool that requires task-based execution cannot be used.
justification: Third-party fact: the Go MCP SDK chosen by DH-LIB-MCP has no task support and lists it as future work; implementing the extension outside the SDK would mean owning part of the protocol. Such a tool is not registered and is counted in the server status, so the model is never offered a tool it cannot call. Revisit when the SDK adds tasks.

reason: A probe of an MCP server lists at most a configured number of pages and tool names and reports truncation.
justification: Deliberate bound on work done for an untrusted server (DH-ADR-CONNECT-2) and on what a management page renders, as outcome DH-O-14 requires; both numbers are configuration (DH-D-CONNECT-2). DH-ADR-CONNECT-2 now states it in its tradeoff (a probe is capped in time and in tools listed).

reason: MCP resource subscriptions and update notifications are not followed; the model lists or reads again for current content.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONNECT-4, the same as unit mcp-client.1: no subscription request is ever sent (test DH-T-CONNECT-22), and a logged resource-changed notice through the context pipeline is named there as a later step (register entry U-K1-7).

reason: A binary MCP resource that is audio or another non-image type is shown to the model as a description.
justification: Deliberate boundary of the model vocabulary, the same as unit mcp-client.4 (DH-ADR-LLM-1 has no audio block); the image half is removed by DH-D-CONNECT-3. DH-ADR-LLM-1 now states the exclusion of audio and video in words.

reason: HTML that nests too deeply or fails to convert is replaced by a fixed omission marker, and table spans are not represented.
justification: Deliberate safety boundary required by the HTML-to-Markdown library specification (DH-LIB-TURNDOWN: raw markup is never the fallback and a span never multiplies work). The span half is also a format fact: Markdown tables have no spanning cell. DH-ADR-CONNECT-8 now states it (HTML that cannot be converted safely becomes an omission marker and is never passed through).

reason: web_search takes queries and an optional region, and web_fetch only a url; the result count is an operator bound and there is no format or summarising mode.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-CONNECT-8 (the two tools keep their minimal arguments beyond the ones named there), so that the tool schema stays the same under every provider (outcome DH-O-10); the full text of a truncated page is kept by the spill policy.

reason: Upstream's shared request cannot pass the vendor Search API's localization parameter. The Go request has an optional region that a provider declares and honours, and the result says whether it was applied (DH-ADR-CONNECT-8, which names this parameter; register entry U-K1-9). Built by DH-D-CONNECT-6 and DH-D-CONNECT-8, proven by DH-T-CONNECT-23. The provider still does not read the service's site and ranking fields: the seam's result has no use for them, and the summary length the bullet measures is bounded by the tool's summary cap.
A fetched PDF is not decoded as text: it is stored as an attachment and reaches the model as page images through the document tool; every other binary type is refused.
justification: Partly removed and partly kept on purpose. Removed: upstream refused a PDF outright; DH-ADR-CONNECT-8 now gives the fetch body a file arm, so a PDF within a size bound is stored after the same address guard and redirect rules and the result names the tool that reads it (DH-D-CONNECT-7, test DH-T-CONNECT-23; register entry U-K1-8); a missing content type is sniffed. Kept: the text decoding that upstream named as deferred work. DH-ADR-CONNECT-8 states that no text extractor is used and that every other binary type stays refused; no pure-Go PDF text extractor has been verified, so adding one is not a small cost. Consequence: a route whose model takes no images cannot read a fetched PDF. The audit (Q3-6) found that the earlier resolved row hid this remainder.

reason: When bytes are valid both as UTF-8 and as another encoding and no declaration settles it, UTF-8 is chosen.
justification: Fact of text encodings: no algorithm identifies an encoding from ambiguous bytes; a detector can only guess. The Go design reads the HTML meta declaration first, which narrows the cases, and keeps upstream's rule of never guessing a legacy encoding (DH-D-CONNECT-7).

reason: A search through the model-backed provider costs one full model request in latency and tokens.
justification: Third-party fact: it is how the vendor's server-side search tool works. The direct Search API provider (DH-D-CONNECT-8) is the alternative, and the unit budget bounds the server-side searches of this provider (DH-D-CONNECT-11). Source: upstream's own bullet (packages/web/web-search-deepseek/README.md, limit 1).

reason: The model-backed search service returns more sources than asked for and the seam truncates afterwards.
justification: Third-party fact: the vendor's wire has no result-count parameter, so the bound can only be applied to the response. This provider is DH-D-CONNECT-11; the direct Search API provider (DH-D-CONNECT-8) is not affected. Source: upstream's own bullet (packages/web/web-search-deepseek/README.md, limit 5).

reason: Whether a source has a snippet depends on what the endpoint returns.
justification: Third-party fact: an endpoint that returns neither an excerpt nor a citation leaves nothing to show. The provider reads structured result blocks only and never scrapes prose, a rule kept for safety; an answer with no source at all is returned as a zero-source result flagged unsourced (DH-D-CONNECT-11, test DH-T-CONNECT-24). Source: upstream's own bullet (packages/web/web-search-deepseek/README.md, limit 6).

reason: Upstream's search request carries no controls. The Go request has an optional region; each provider declares which controls it honours and the result reports each control as applied or ignored, with one tool schema under every provider (DH-ADR-CONNECT-8; register entry U-K1-9). Built by DH-D-CONNECT-6 and proven by DH-T-CONNECT-23. Recency and site filters are added when a backend honours them, by the same decision.
The fetch body has a file arm that carries a stored PDF, but no arm for text extracted from a PDF.
justification: Upstream's bullet names text-extractable PDF support as the deferred work behind the missing arm. The Go body type gains a file arm that carries a stored PDF as an attachment reference with its size and the name of the reading tool (DH-D-CONNECT-6, test DH-T-CONNECT-23; register entry U-K1-8), and DH-ADR-CONNECT-8 states that no text extractor is used, so the text arm stays out by that record. The same remainder as unit web-fetch-http.2.

reason: Provider-backed page extraction (a hosted service that returns cleaned page content) is not part of the web seam.
justification: Deliberate boundary now stated by DH-ADR-CONNECT-8: no hosted page-extraction service is a provider, because it would send the page's address to a third party the user did not choose.

reason: The model cannot switch the browser backend; configuration selects the one provider.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-MEDIA-1 (no tool argument can select a provider, an endpoint or a mode): otherwise the model, or text injected into a page, could select attach mode and with it the user's own logged-in browser.

reason: The model cannot switch the computer-use driver; configuration selects the one provider.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-MEDIA-1: which software controls the user's desktop is an operator decision and never a tool argument (see also owner decision DH-ADR-19).

reason: Rendering, fonts and pagination follow LibreOffice and can differ from Microsoft Office, and between two machines with different installs.
justification: Third-party fact: no design in the harness makes one layout engine reproduce another, and owner decision DH-ADR-20 fixes an operator-installed LibreOffice as the engine. Every result names the engine version and missing fonts are reported (DH-ADR-MEDIA-2).

reason: The vendor account protocol issues tokens with no expiry or refresh and accepts a loopback callback address only.
justification: Third-party fact: redirect addresses and token lifetime are decided by the vendor service, not by the client. The design adds what it can: sign-out removes the local grant first and then revokes, a pending revocation is not kept on disk because that would keep the old token, and the user is told when issuer revocation failed (DH-ADR-HUMAN-10, DH-ADR-HUMAN-11).

reason: A stored key is reported as configured by presence alone; a wrong key is found out when the provider rejects it or when the user runs the route check.
justification: Deliberate boundary: nothing leaves the machine unasked (owner decision DH-ADR-9, DH-ADR-HUMAN-11), so no background validity check is made. The user-started check that the interaction spec lists as a request to the model area already exists there: the on-demand route check of DH-D-LLM-4 sends one small real request and reports the classified result.

reason: The launch environment is a snapshot taken at start, so a variable exported later in the launching shell is not seen.
justification: Operating-system fact: a running process cannot observe a later change to its parent shell's environment on any system. The layers that can change, the two .env files and stored values, are watched and apply without a restart (DH-D-HUMAN-7).

reason: A credential reference is an environment-variable-shaped name in one flat namespace.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-9 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: a credential reference is an environment-shaped name in one flat namespace, never a path or a structured key; a credential with structure, such as a sign-in grant, is a record under owner and id), because one namespace lets the same name be set in the launch environment, a .env file or the store.

reason: No notification can be raised for a variable changed in the launching shell, so a page that shows an environment-sourced credential learns of a change only after a restart.
justification: Operating-system fact, the same as unit credentials-local.3. Changes to stored values and to the .env files do raise a change notice, including for another process on the same home (DH-D-HUMAN-7).

reason: A feedback entry carries one category and one text and has no severity field.
justification: Deliberate boundary: no consumer in the design ranks feedback, so a severity field would be data nobody reads; it can be added under a new payload version. DH-ADR-HUMAN-13 now states it (an entry has a category and no severity). The referenced-event half of the upstream bullet is removed by DH-D-HUMAN-10.

reason: Deleting a rating or withdrawing a remark removes the current item only; earlier values stay in the session log.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-1: the append-only log is the single source of truth and committed events are immutable. Erasure is deleting the session, which the session store provides (DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-10).

reason: Upstream refuses a feedback change when another process holds the session. In the Go design the home database has a request table (DH-ADR-STORE-12, the owner's resolution of register entry U-K1-5 in DH-ADR-40): a process that does not hold the session files the change, the holder applies it as its own append in the transaction that marks the request applied, and a request nobody applies expires and the user is told. The feedback service is the first user, through session.Service.AppendLogOnly (DH-ADR-SESSION-12, DH-ADR-HUMAN-13). Built by DH-D-STORE-11 and DH-D-SESSION-9; proven by DH-T-STORE-17 and the request step of scenario DH-E-STORE-1.
Resetting or losing the anonymous identifier creates a new identity that cannot be linked to the old one.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-12: this is the anonymity property itself; recovery would need stable material derived from the machine or the user.

reason: Two harness homes have unrelated anonymous identifiers and cannot be correlated.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-12 in its own words (Scope boundary of this record: the identifier belongs to one harness home; two homes of the same person have two identifiers and nothing links them, because a link would need an account or a shared secret, which is the identity the anonymous identifier exists to avoid).

reason: A command handler must honour cancellation; one that does not is settled as aborted after a grace period and tracked as detached.
justification: Go runtime fact, the same as tools unit tool-executor-native.1: a goroutine cannot be stopped from outside. DH-ADR-HUMAN-8 bounds the wait and reports the detached handler instead of hiding it.

reason: A permission preset bundles two knobs, sandbox mode and approval policy, and does not choose the agent composition.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-6 (a preset bundles two knobs): which tools and prompt an agent has is the agent preset; folding it into the Permissions choice would make one control change both authority and capability.

reason: The reserved auto preset cannot be the default for new sessions.
justification: Deliberate boundary under DH-ADR-HUMAN-6: auto is contributed by an experimental, default-off review component, and a default that names an entry which may not be loaded would leave new sessions without a valid permission state.

reason: The default preset must name an entry of the preset table, so removing that entry and changing the default happen in one configuration edit.
justification: Deliberate fail-closed rule under DH-ADR-HUMAN-6: falling back to some other preset when the named default disappears would change a security default without the operator saying so. An edit that breaks the rule is rejected with its position.

reason: Upstream refuses a question from a subagent outright. In the Go design every item a child agent raises is registered for its own session and offered to whoever answers for the root session of its tree, labelled with the child's path, and settles unavailable if the root has no answerer (rule 5 of who may answer, DH-ADR-HUMAN-2; DH-ADR-SUBAGENT-6). The owner confirmed on 2026-11-19 that a subagent's request goes to whoever answers for the root session (DH-ADR-16), and both specifications now say so.
A pending approval is not restored after a host restart; on resume the open audit pair is closed as unavailable and the call is denied.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-1 (pending approvals live in memory only) and DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-10: the interrupted turn is closed and never continued, so there is no call left to approve.

reason: A question is selectable options plus optional text; file pickers and diff confirmations have no interaction kind.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HUMAN-1 (four closed kinds): each kind needs a payload type, a rendered fragment and a mapping in the SDK and ACP protocols, so a kind is added when a tool needs it.

reason: Unfinished answer text stays in the browser tab that holds it and is not stored by the host.
justification: Deliberate boundary: a draft is not a decision, and storing keystrokes of an unanswered question would add a write path and a second copy to keep consistent across tabs. DH-ADR-HUMAN-1 now states it in its tradeoff (a half-typed answer stays in the browser tab that holds it).

reason: A vendor business failure is shown with its numeric code and a generic message; specific wording per code is missing.
justification: Still open (register entry U-K1-12): the list of business codes and the wording for each are not in the pinned upstream source, and the convergence round added nothing for it. The message catalogue is keyed by code, so wording can be added without a code change. What is missing: the vendor's list, and a named step (a scenario or an owner action) that obtains it.

reason: Upstream finds a macOS application only in known directories. DH-ADR-HOST-9 now also runs one Spotlight query by bundle identifier (/usr/bin/mdfind) through the host starter, at resolution time only, with a deadline and bounded output, and accepts a result only if its Info.plist names the same identifier (audit finding Q3-11). Built by DH-D-HOST-9; proven by DH-T-HOST-28 (a fake starter finds an entry outside the known directories, ignores a mismatched identifier, and survives a timeout) and by scenario DH-E-HOST-10 with an editor moved out of /Applications. Remainder: an application Spotlight does not index is added by an operator entry, as the record says.
No application icons are extracted; the UI shows a category glyph and the application's name.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HOST-9 (application icons are not extracted): extraction needs a platform helper or a native API on each system, for a decoration.

reason: The queue for analytics and telemetry records is memory-only: overflow, a failed request and process exit lose records. The loss is counted and shown.
justification: Deliberate boundary stated by DH-ADR-HOST-7: a durable outbox would store usage data on disk and would have to be purged when the user withdraws consent (owner decision DH-ADR-9 makes all of it opt-in). A consumer that needs delivery, the session upload, keeps its own progress in the session log.

reason: The request carries the session as an opaque label, Meta.Session, declared in the leaf package llm/vocab. Package session imports that leaf and package llm imports session, so there is no import cycle and no duplicate declaration; an import-direction test enforces it.
The preset component accepts a configuration update in place and notifies permission.CatalogChanged, so the table can change without reloading the component.

Upstream ships no answerer in a headless or incompletely composed deployment, so every approval there fails without anyone being asked.
